pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.en: house
table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.en: hello
Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.en: boy
street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.en: but
dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.en: thanks
coffee

alphabet.title: The Spanish alphabet: 27 letters
alphabet.explain: Spanish uses the same letters as English plus Ñ. Letter names matter for spelling your name aloud. Read each name, then say the example word.

letters.tip: soft, like TH in this: DÍA
Y in yes, or EE alone: YO

counting.title: Counting 0 to 100
counting.explain: Learn 0–15 by heart. 16–19 = DIEZ + number stuck together (dieciséis). 20s = VEINTI + number (veintidós). 30+ = tens + Y + ones (treinta y uno). 100 = CIEN (cien alone, ciento + more).
rules: 30–99 use Y: treinta y uno (31), cuarenta y dos (42).
CIEN = exactly 100; CIENTO + more: ciento uno (101).
